# Popover

Popover owns popup state and explicit focus or dismissal effects.

## Basic usage

Popover demonstrates anchored as a separate, interactive configuration.

<ComponentExample component="popover" scenario="anchored" title="Popover" description="Popover demonstrates anchored as a separate, interactive configuration." :index="0" />

## Features

- Open state.
- Non modal dialog semantics.
- Outside dismissal.
- Escape close.
- Focus restoration.
- Anchored placement.
- Collision flip.
- Controlled open.

Each feature is part of the public semantic contract. Host packages may expose different input and rendering helpers while preserving accepted transitions.

### Controlled

The parent owns the current value and applies every accepted change back to Popover.

### Closed

Popover starts closed and opens only from its trigger.

## State ownership

State that changes application-owned data supports controlled or uncontrolled ownership where the component contract permits it. Use uncontrolled state for local behavior and controlled state when a parent coordinates validation, persistence, or multiple controls.

## Disabled and readonly

Host projections distinguish disabled interaction from readonly inspection when the underlying control permits both. Disabled controls leave the interaction sequence; readonly controls remain available for inspection while rejecting mutation.

## Semantics

The component contract follows [the relevant accessibility pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/). Visual styling remains outside the package; use host attributes, parts, and state projections as styling hooks.
